general_information.Description: The course which is a continuation of OFC311, first covers the design methods of digital links and analog links over optical fiber. Second it addresses the principles of wavelength division multiplexing (WDM), examines the functions of a genetic WDM links and discusses international standards for different WDM schemes. Subsequently, the course describes different concepts for creating optical amplification and show how the elements are put together to form links and networks. Then, optical networking concepts for long-haul, metro, local area, and access networks are presented. Finally, the performance measurement and mornitoring for optical fiber links which are very important to manage error, fault and maintenance are introduced. Topics are covered: Digital Links; Analog Link; WDM Concepts and Components; Optical Amplifiers; Nonlinear Effects; Optical Networks; Performance Measurement and Monitoring.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises and assignments given by an instructor in class or at home and submit on time. - Constantly follow announcements on intranet/CMS at http://cms.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information.
general_information.Tools: Modeling and Simulation Tools: (suggestion) 1. Optiwave, http://www.optiwave.com (recommended) 2. RSoft Design Group, http://www.rsoftdesign.com 3. VPIsystems, http://www.vpiphotonics.com

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Focus on main impacts of optical fiber communications: Attenuation and Dispersion
assessments.Grading Guide: 1. Each lab activity can be assigned for every group of 3-4 students 2. The lab manual can be download from the website: Lab 1: http://optiwave.com/resources/applications-resources/optical-system-lesson-3-optical-systems-wdm-design/ AND Lab 2,3,4: http://optiwave.com/resources/academia/optisystem-lab-assignments/ 3. Analysis and Report: Compare the results of the simulations and your pre-lab calculations and record your observations and explanations of differences in your lab report. 4. Your report should contain: • Cover page - Title of the lab - Course name - Your name and student number • Pre-lab calculations • Screen shots of layout and results, including eye diagrams • Summary table listing for each simulation which is required fully in the manual. For example: Lab 1: - Fiber length in km - Received power in dBm - Q factor - BER • Written summary of your observations and your analysis
assessments.Note: - Reports must be submitted at the end of every pratical session. - Instructor should supervise everygroup's progress in the practical session to ensure all tasks done and no-cheating - The lab evaluation is averagely based on group progress in the practical sessions and the group reports. The scores should be finished before the final examination

assessments.Grading Guide: - Test 1: cover chapter 8 and 9 - Test 2: cover chapter 10 and 11 - Test 3: cover chapter 12, 13 and 14 Each test should have both theory questions and numerial problems covering contents of every chapter equally
